questions.question: Statement: "The bank will remain closed on the second Saturday of every month." Conclusions: I. The bank remains closed at least one Saturday every month. II. The bank is closed on more days than it opens.
questions.rationale: The second Saturday is certainly one Saturday, so I follows. II invents a comparison over all days of the month that the statement never makes, so it does not follow.

questions.question: Statement: "Shyam scored higher than Ravi, and Ravi scored higher than Mohan." Which conclusion definitely follows?
options: Mohan scored the lowest of the three
Ravi scored the highest of the three
questions.rationale: Higher-than is transitive, so Shyam is above Ravi, who is above Mohan; with three people in that order, Mohan is necessarily last. The other options contradict or reverse this order.

questions.question: Statement: "Regular practice of meditation helps reduce stress." Conclusions: I. People who practise meditation may experience less stress. II. Meditation is the best cure for stress.
questions.rationale: I is the statement weakened from "helps" to "may", and weaker options always follow. II invents a superlative comparison with every other cure that the statement never attempted.

questions.question: Statement: "The government has banned single-use plastic bags in the city." Conclusions: I. Using single-use plastic bags is now prohibited in the city. II. The city will become completely free of plastic waste.
questions.rationale: A ban prohibits exactly what it names, so I follows directly. II escalates one product ban into a total plastic-free claim — an over-generalisation the statement never licenses.

questions.question: Statements: "All students of Class X attended the science fair. Some students who attended the fair won prizes." Conclusions: I. Every Class X student was present at the fair. II. Some Class X students won prizes.
questions.rationale: I restates the first statement exactly. II fails because the prize winners could all belong to other classes that also attended — the statements never connect the prizes to Class X students.

questions.question: Statement: "Only graduates are eligible for this post." Conclusions: I. A candidate who is not a graduate is not eligible. II. Every graduate is eligible for this post.
questions.rationale: "Only graduates" makes graduation a necessary condition, which is precisely I. But necessary is not sufficient — graduates may still fail other requirements — so II overstates the rule.

questions.question: Statement: "Some ministers are honest." Conclusions: I. Some ministers are dishonest. II. It cannot be said that no minister is honest.
questions.rationale: "Some" never licenses the opposite fact, so I does not follow. II is strictly weaker than the statement — if some are honest, then it is false that none are — so II follows.

questions.question: Statement: "All successful people work hard." Conclusions: I. All people who work hard are successful. II. Success is not possible without hard work.
questions.rationale: I reverses the "all" direction — an invalid conversion, since hard workers may still fail. II is the contrapositive in plain words: every successful person works hard, so no success can occur without it.

questions.question: Statement: "The number of road accidents dropped after speed cameras were installed on the highway." Conclusions: I. Speed cameras may have contributed to the reduction. II. Speed cameras are the only way to reduce accidents.
questions.rationale: I merely allows the connection the timing suggests, at "may" strength, so it follows. II converts one measure into the only possible measure — an extreme claim the statement never supports.

questions.question: Statement: "The city's air quality worsened every winter for the last five years." Which conclusion definitely follows?
options: The city's air quality can never improve
The city's air quality is worst in summer
The city's air quality tends to worsen in winter
The government is responsible for the pollution
questions.rationale: A five-year winter pattern supports the modest seasonal claim at "tends to" strength. "Never" and "worst in summer" overshoot the data, and responsibility for pollution is a new fact the statement never gave.
